reference_sql:
WITH gaps AS (
  -- one row per app event from 09:00 to 10:00 UTC on 4 November 2025
  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
    LAG(event_ts) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id ORDER BY event_ts, event_id) AS prev_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 09:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 10:00:00+00'
)
SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts,
  CASE WHEN prev_ts IS NULL OR event_ts - prev_ts > INTERVAL '30 minutes' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS new_session
FROM gaps

WITH hour_events AS (
  -- one row per app event from 09:00 to 10:00 UTC on 4 November 2025
  SELECT event_id, user_id, event_ts
  FROM app_events
  WHERE event_ts >= TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 09:00:00+00'
    AND event_ts < TIMESTAMPTZ '2025-11-04 10:00:00+00'
)
SELECT e.event_id, e.user_id, e.event_ts,
  CASE WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM hour_events p WHERE p.user_id = e.user_id AND p.event_ts < e.event_ts
    AND p.event_ts >= e.event_ts - INTERVAL '30 minutes') THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS new_session
FROM hour_events e

other_way.tradeoff: Asking whether the user had another event in the 30 minutes before works without LAG, but it searches the hour again for each event.
